intent: Candidate identity-resolution strategies compared on the axes that matter; the recommendation is LOCKED 2026-06-17. Option A (deterministic-first with heuristic recovery) is the Phase 1 build. Option B (ML-blended scoring) is not a rejected alternative — it is the Phase 2 evolution, deferred until curation under Option A produces the labeled training data an ML matcher needs; the heuristic recovery layer is the seam it slots into. First-principles design: DAS has no cross-system resolution today; Common Client ID is one candidate signal and the migration key, never the foundation. Owners: Alicia + Luis.

options.title: Option A — Deterministic-first with heuristic recovery
options.summary: Deterministic exact-match on normalized email / phone (E.164) / VIN / per-dealer customer ID resolves the unambiguous majority. No-match and ambiguous events fall through to a heuristic recovery layer (blocking + scoring + human curation queue), which doubles as the training-data source for Phase 2 ML. Common Client ID is one weighted signal and the migration/backfill key, never the join foundation. Orphan identifiers are stored with attribution and resolved later when a linking event arrives.

positions.matching: Deterministic waterfall on normalized email → phone (E.164) → VIN → per-dealer customer ID for the high-confidence majority. No-match events fall through to heuristic recovery: blocking on phonetic name + canonical address + locality, scored against feature-engineered candidates. Configurable thresholds split outcomes into auto-merge (high), curation queue (medium), and no-link (low). Phase 1 ships rule-based scoring; Phase 2 swaps in the pairwise classifier behind the same interface — no schema migration.
positions.orphans: First-class storage with attribution and no consumer_id until linkable. identity_link retains the orphan with link_type='orphan' plus source, event_id, and observed_at. Late resolution: when a later event carries the orphan ID alongside a deterministic key (e.g., a Meta lead form delivers email + Facebook ID), the orphan is upgraded to deterministic or heuristic link without losing the original audit trail. Never discarded.
positions.provenance: Per-element source attribution at the core-entity level — every field carries source, method (deterministic | heuristic | curated | gnn_cluster | manual_merge), confidence, event_id, observed_at. Per-tenant isolation via PostgreSQL RLS is the working assumption; the data model is RLS-ready but the isolation primitive itself is owned by the Privacy-by-Design deliverable and may be refined.
positions.curation: Ambiguous events (medium-confidence scored matches, or multiple candidates above threshold) land in a side-by-side conflict review queue. Human operator picks merge / reject / defer; the decision writes to merge_history with full audit trail and becomes Phase 2 training data. Queue volume is an open Phase 0 question — sized after the first weeks of live traffic; Phase 1 ships with manual SLAs and revisits after measurement.
positions.migration: CCID is one weighted signal in the deterministic waterfall (weight set by the DWRPT audit in progress) and the primary key for historical-record backfill. Cutover: mint consumer_ids keyed to CCID where present, retain CCID on the entity as a legacy identifier (not a join key), and let the deterministic waterfall collapse duplicates surfaced across CCID-anchored records. Records without CCID coverage backfill via the waterfall directly. No production read path depends on CCID after cutover.
positions.ops: Fast path: synchronous deterministic lookup returns consumer_id from indexed normalized identifiers (target sub-100ms p95). Heuristic recovery runs async — inbound events are best-effort linked or queued, never blocked. Idempotency by event_id; reprocessing is safe because deterministic results are stable. Phase 1 cost profile is index-driven on the fast path and batch/queue-driven for recovery; no real-time ML inference.

options.title: Option B — ML-blended scoring (Phase 2 evolution)
options.summary: The Phase 2 destination, not a competing Phase 1 design. Once curation under Option A has produced enough labeled merge decisions, the heuristic recovery layer is replaced by a single feature-scored matching model: exact identifier matches become strong features; weaker signals (phonetic name, address tokens, behavioral co-occurrence) score proportionally; threshold bucketing routes into auto-merge / curation / no-link — no deterministic / heuristic split. It is the wrong answer for Phase 1 only because the training data does not exist yet; the analysis below records why, and what must be true before it is worth doing. This is when we actually do the ML bits.

positions.matching: Single feature-scored matcher (likely Splink-class probabilistic record linkage, or a trained classifier) consumes every event. Features include exact-match flags (email, phone, VIN, dealer customer ID), phonetic name distance, canonicalized address tokens, behavioral co-occurrence, CCID match. Scorer outputs a probability; thresholds bucket into auto-merge / queue / no-link. No deterministic-vs-heuristic split — matching policy lives in one place. Cold-start risk: DAS has no cross-system merge history to train on (zero cross-system resolution today per kickoff). Bootstrapping from labeled exact-match cases teaches trivial pairs only — Phase 1 effectively ships rules dressed as ML until real curation labels accumulate.
positions.orphans: Identical handling to Option A — stored with attribution under link_type='orphan' plus source, event_id, observed_at; upgraded when a later event carries a linkable key. Orphan management is structural, not model-dependent.
positions.provenance: Per-element source / method / confidence / event_id / observed_at, same shape as Option A. method='ml_scored' with model_version as first-class metadata; reprocessing under a newer model is a normal flow. Explainability tradeoff: 'exact email match' is auditable on its own; 'score 0.87 because features X/Y/Z' requires the model + feature attribution to defend. Counts against the visible-golden-record validation conversation Mike asked for (2026-06-12 sync).
positions.curation: Same side-by-side review queue as Option A, but it fires on every medium-confidence score — not just no-match events. Threshold tuning is the operator's primary dial. Curated decisions feed model retraining; the queue is the data engine. Volume risk: until thresholds settle, the queue can flood, and there is no measurement to size operator capacity from until after launch. Operational risk concentrated in Phase 1.
positions.migration: CCID is a strong feature input to the scorer (not a join key). Backfill: rescore historical records through the trained model; CCID-anchored records become high-score deterministic-equivalent matches. Records without CCID coverage resolve through the same model as new traffic. Cutover risk concentrated in initial model quality — a bad cold-start affects every backfilled record, with no deterministic baseline to fall back to.
positions.ops: Real-time model inference on every event — target sub-300ms p95 vs sub-100ms for Option A's index lookups. Inference cost on every event vs Option A's mostly-index-only fast path; at DAS volume (RL_PROD.oltp = 1.13B rows; hundreds of millions of events/year) this compounds. Idempotency by (event_id, model_version) — rescoring is normal. Failure mode: no deterministic fallback layer — model regressions affect every record. Day-one operational stack required: model versioning, drift monitoring, retrain cadence, threshold-tuning runbook, shadow rollout. Ongoing ML expertise dependency for the life of the system.

recommendation.note: Option A locked for Phase 1. The decisive factor is cold-start training data: DAS has no cross-system merge history to train an ML matcher on, so Option B's Phase 1 model would effectively be rules dressed as ML — with day-one operational overhead (model versioning, drift, threshold tuning) and no deterministic fallback when the model is wrong. Option A produces curated training data through normal operation, and the heuristic recovery layer is the natural seam where the Phase 2 ML matcher slots in once labels exist; at that point Option A converges toward Option B with real training data behind it. Option B becomes the right answer once curation has been running long enough to produce meaningful labels — that is a Phase 2 conversation, not a Phase 0 commitment. Locked 2026-06-17 by Luis with Alicia's concurrence.
